summary: Requested one focused fan-out experiment for the decided-subscription defect: ten decided entries, trim to 5, and two simulated subscriber cursors (slow at 1, fast at 6) driven by the actor's push_to_all_subs arithmetic over real read_decided_suffix outputs. Prediction: the fast subscriber receives entry 10 for cursor 6 (skipping 7–9) and 10 again later, so a lagging peer can make other subscribers silently skip decided entries — a stronger consequence than the single-subscriber duplicate already witnessed. The snapshot-path knowledge entry and all prior defect accounts stand; this experiment is pending.
